title: Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (Act No. 35 of 2019)
issuing_authority: Ministry of Law and Justice / Legislative Department
description: The foundational legislation replacing the 1986 Act, establishing the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA), introducing product liability, strict rules on misleading ads, and enabling electronic filing.

title: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020
issuing_authority: Department of Consumer Affairs, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
description: Rules governing marketplace and inventory e-commerce entities, regulating cancellation fees, mandatory appointment of grievance officers, transparency of prices, country of origin, and return rules.

title: Guidelines for Prevention of Misleading Advertisements and Endorsements, 2022
description: Defines parameters for valid advertisements, bait advertisements, surrogate ads, free claim ads, disclaimers, and establishes duties and due diligence required of endorsers and manufacturers.

title: National Consumer Helpline (NCH) Pre-Litigation Grievance Redressal
issuing_authority: Department of Consumer Affairs & Indian Institute of Public Administration (IIPA)
description: Pre-litigation helpline operating over 1000+ converged corporate entities for speedy resolution without filing court petitions. Reachable via 1915, WhatsApp, SMS, or UMANG app.

title: e-Daakhil: Consumer Commission Online Filing Portal Manual
issuing_authority: National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) / National Informatics Centre (NIC)
description: Digital platform enabling consumers to electronically file petitions, pay court fees via Bharatkosh, submit rejoinders, and inspect proceeding cause lists across District, State, and National Commissions.

title: Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission, State Commission and National Commission) Rules, 2021
description: Revised pecuniary limits for consumer commissions: District Commission up to ₹50 Lakh, State Commission above ₹50 Lakh to ₹2 Crore, and National Commission above ₹2 Crore (calculated on consideration paid).
key_sections: Rule 2 (Jurisdiction determination based on consideration paid)
